extracted.intended_audience: federal agency standards managers, policy makers, and NIST/ICSP staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting on how Federal agencies should participate in, adopt, track, and manage voluntary consensus standards under the NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119. Covers agency policy elements, staff preparation, coordination with SDOs/ANSI, state/local coordination, conformity assessment, and information systems for tracking participation and adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue and increase use of voluntary standards for procurement and regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Most Federal agencies have already made significant progress in their use of voluntary standards for agency programs and missions. This trend should be vigorously continued for both procurement and regulatory activities. Agencies should increase their participation in those activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are expected to continue and expand use of private-sector voluntary consensus standards in procurement and regulatory contexts where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop agency policy and programmatic elements to implement NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should develop specific policy and programmatic elements to support the implementation of the NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements for consideration include establishment of agency standards policy and units for monitoring standards activities; resource allocation; infrastructure; reporting; and assessing program effectiveness (as presented in the ICF Kaiser report prepared for EPA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan participation based on agency strategic needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should consider their own strategic needs when planning for agency participation in standards activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available resources, including NIST, to determine applicable Standards Developing Organizations (SDOs) (national and international), relevant voluntary standards, and the need for new standards in emerging technologies and processes. NIST should facilitate interactions between agencies and the voluntary standards process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and coordinate agency views and positions for committee participation
rubrics_metrics.description: ICSP should develop guidelines for use when agencies prepare staff for participation in standards-related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines should reflect the need to prepare agency views and coordinate positions with other relevant agencies so that all Federal needs are reflected; appropriate activities in committees to avoid the appearance of dominance; and consideration of likely future agency and national needs during development and revision of voluntary standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve and use systems to track standards adoption and staff participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies should improve and utilize systems for tracking the adoption or referencing of voluntary standards, as well as the level of staff participation in voluntary standards-developing bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should use electronic means for setting up directory databases of participants and exchanging information about standards-related issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Strategic Standards Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategic standards management is defined as setting organizational needs, priorities, and strategies for participating in the development and use of voluntary standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It requires identification of resources to meet organizational needs, target areas for developing or revising voluntary standards, and coordination of standards positions, policies, and votes within an organization. Develop strategic standards management plans and procedures (NIST and agency-level).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with state and local governments on standards implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIST is working with state and local agencies to identify and develop procedures for using and implementing voluntary standards, and to identify organizations and stakeholders who can contribute and benefit from coordinated efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include establishing an oversight council to advise states/localities, developing cooperative agreements, conducting workshops/conferences to educate state/local agencies, and forming a State-Federal Partnership to address knowledge gaps and implementation of the NTTAA at state/local levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate and engage with SDOs and ANSI
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (and NIST) should coordinate with Standards Developing Organizations and ANSI to support standards use and policy development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include attending and participating in ANSI boards/councils and other SDO meetings on overarching policy issues; sponsoring conferences on federal use of voluntary standards; supporting NSSN (National Standards Service Network) web-based information resources and procuring site-wide licenses to enhance access to standards information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate conformity assessment activities and reduce redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate conformity assessment activities (e.g., laboratory accreditation) to recognize competence and reduce redundant, duplicative conformity assessment activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST actions include hosting open forums (e.g., for formation of NACLA), creating operational procedures for a public/private coordination body, establishing programs such as the Accrediting Body Evaluation Program (ABEP), implementing National Voluntary Conformity Assessment System Evaluation (NVGASE), and operating NVLAP to carry out accreditations in support of federal laws and agency needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use voluntary consensus standards in place of duplicative FIPS
rubrics_metrics.description: FIPS are reviewed to ensure they are up-to-date and still needed; FIPS that duplicate current voluntary industry standards are withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies are directed by the NTTAA (P.L. 104-113) to use technical standards developed in voluntary consensus standards bodies; therefore there is no longer a need to establish FIPS that duplicate available industry standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt voluntary standards when they enhance regulatory mission and harmonization
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (e.g., FDA) participate in and adopt or use standards when this action will enhance their ability to protect consumers and the effectiveness or efficiency of regulatory efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using standards, especially international ones, facilitates harmonization of regulatory requirements with foreign governments and furthers domestic and global public health. Agencies may still use government-unique standards when none are available or appropriate to meet regulatory protection levels (examples: food/color additives, pesticides, certain veterinary products).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and disseminate participation data via central directories (SAMI/NCSCI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments should collect and disseminate information on staff participation in outside standards-writing activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SAMI project and NCSCI maintain directories and reference collections with statistics on committee participation, participant listings, standards organizations/committees, translations, and alerts on draft foreign standards; agencies are encouraged to provide additional participation information to these resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace government-unique standards with voluntary standards when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and substitute voluntary consensus standards for government-unique standards as a result of agency review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: DoD reports dozens of government specifications and standards replaced by voluntary standards (lists of MIL and MS specifications and their ASTM/SAE/ANSI replacements). Agencies should follow review processes to identify such substitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow OMB Circular A-119 Section 7 guidance on interacting with voluntary consensus standards bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 7 of the proposed revision to OMB Circular A-119 provides guidelines for using voluntary consensus standards bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As written, this section reinforces current agency policies regarding use of voluntary standards, reliance on performance documents, and encouragement of participation in voluntary standards bodies; agencies should evaluate the effectiveness of these guidelines for their standards management programs and recommend changes if needed.
